_comment: Per-host access requirements. Every entry is a documented thing the site asks of
ordinary visitors - an age gate, a consent cookie, a slower pace - never a disguise.
The user agent is not settable here and spider.py exits if an entry tries.
If a host refuses the identified crawler, that refusal is recorded as a null.
It is not worked around from this file.

justice.gov.why: The site sets an age-verification cookie on its own interstitial before serving documents. This is the same cookie a browser would carry after clicking through. Some pages (seen on usao-ma and usao-sdny press releases, 21 and 24 Sept 2026) answer with an Akamai bot-challenge interstitial - HTTP 200, ~2.5 KB, blank title, a bm-verify meta refresh. That is a refusal, not a document: it is matched by marker and recorded as a null. It is never solved. The archive path justice.gov/archive/usao/... often serves the real page.

efts.sec.gov.why: EDGAR full-text search asks automated clients to identify themselves and to stay under 10 requests a second. The identification is the standing user agent; the pace is set here well below the limit.

www.sec.gov.why: Same EDGAR fair-access policy as efts.sec.gov.

jmail.world.why: The www host 307-redirects to the apex. Redirects are followed, which is all this needs; recorded here so the behaviour is not mistaken for a fault.

irp.fas.org.why: A small volunteer-run archive holding primary government documents. The delay is deliberately generous - it costs us nothing and the mirror is load-bearing for this project.

www.cia.gov.why: The reading room is a JavaScript application: node/ and print/ document ids return the homepage to any plain HTTP client, ours included. That is a rendering limit, not a block, and no amount of header work changes it. Documents from here are attributed, not primary, until pulled from a mirror that serves HTML. Registered as a decoy title so those 200s are demoted to nulls instead of entering the ledger as sources. Registered 24 Oct 2026 from the FOI source survey (research/sources/FOI-SOURCES.md). Reading-room PDF and document URLs now redirect to a site-wide maintenance page, HTTP 200, 508,740 B.
decoy_titles: Freedom of Information Act Electronic Reading Room

www.b0b.dev.why: Our own access gate answers every path with an 8,607-byte pixel page at HTTP 200, static assets included. Registered so a self-check cannot mistake the gate for the content.

www.federalregister.gov.why: HTML and plain-text document pages redirect plain clients to unblock.federalregister.gov, a 10,596-byte 'Request Access' page, with HTTP 200. The JSON API (/api/v1/documents/) and the govinfo PDF serve the same documents; use those. Registered as a decoy so the 200 is a null, not a source (seen 23 Sept 2026).

www.govinfo.gov.why: Some Weekly Compilation URLs redirect to /error and return a 'Page Not Found | GovInfo' page with HTTP 200 (seen 23 Sept 2026). The package PDFs are reliable.

ohchr.org.why: A PDF path that no longer resolves (seen on the apex host, ohchr.org) 302s to www.ohchr.org/en/ohchr_homepage and serves the homepage, ~138 KB, title 'UN Human Rights Office', with HTTP 200. Real OHCHR PDFs return 200 with no HTML title; the www article pages refuse this crawler with 403. Registered so the homepage is a null, not the document (seen 1 Oct 2026 on A/HRC/63/61).

decoy_markers: Could not find the specified document
media.cadc.uscourts.gov.why: A document path that does not exist returns HTTP 200 with a 158-byte body reading 'Could not find the specified document' instead of a 404, so a mistyped opinion number enters the ledger as a success. Real opinions are PDFs of tens of kilobytes or more. Registered so the stub is a null (seen 2 Oct 2026 on 21-7135, Doe v. Apple).

2021-2025.state.gov.why: The archived State Department site answers document paths (seen on the May 2024 NSM-20 report PDF) with a 188,865-byte HTML page titled 'Technical Difficulties' and HTTP 200, so a missing document enters the ledger as a success. Registered so that page is a null (seen 19 Oct 2026). The current state.gov copy of the same PDF refused this crawler with 403.

uscode.house.gov.why: A section path the site cannot resolve returns a 'Page Not Found - US Code' page with HTTP 200 instead of a 404. Real section pages carry the section number in the title ('22 USC 2776: ...'). Registered so the not-found page is a null (seen 19 Oct 2026). Cornell LII serves the same text.

icc-cpi.int.why: Court-record HTML paths sometimes answer with the CDN's security-check page, title 'Gcore', HTTP 200, instead of the filing. That is a refusal, not a document, and it is never solved. The CourtRecords PDFs (sites/default/files/CourtRecords/...) serve directly. Registered so the check page is a null (seen 19 Oct 2026).

senate.gov.why: An article path the site cannot resolve redirects to /pagelayout/general/one_item_and_teasers/file_not_found.htm and serves it with HTTP 200, title 'U.S. Senate: 404 Error Page'. Real pages carry their subject in the title. Registered so the not-found page is a null (seen 22 Oct 2026 on an Art & History 'Have you no sense of decency' path).

boi.org.il.why: The Bank of Israel's site answers this crawler with Radware's browser-verification page, title 'Radware Page', ~118 KB, HTTP 200, instead of the press releases. That is a refusal, not a document, and it is never solved. Registered so the challenge page is a null (seen 23 Oct 2026).

api.govinfo.gov.why: api.data.gov issues free keys to anyone who signs up; the author is to sign up for one himself (24 Oct 2026; not held at this writing). The key is read from $API_DATA_GOV_KEY and sent as the X-Api-Key header, which api.data.gov accepts in place of the api_key query parameter, so it never appears in a URL or in the public ledger. Without the variable nothing is sent and the service's refusal is recorded as a null. DEMO_KEY (api.data.gov's public demo key, 30 requests an hour) works for a test.
